html:
The Clouds is a comedy by Aristophanes, first staged in Athens in 423 BCE. It mocks the new learning of the day, and it makes Socrates its main target.

An old farmer, Strepsiades, is drowning in debts run up by his horse-mad son. He enrols at the "Thinkery", a school run by Socrates, to learn the clever arguments that will let him cheat his creditors. Socrates first appears hanging in a basket in the air, studying the sky. The school teaches that the gods are clouds, and stages a contest between a Better Argument and a Worse Argument, which the Worse one wins. It all goes wrong, and the play ends with the angry farmer burning the school down.

The play came last of three in its contest. Aristophanes revised it, and the revised text is the one that survives. It lumps Socrates in with the sophists, whom he opposed. Years later, in his account of the trial of Socrates, Plato has Socrates say this kind of comedy had turned people against him long before he was charged.
sum: The Clouds is a comedy by Aristophanes, first staged in Athens in 423 BCE. It mocks the new learning of the day, and it makes Socrates its main target.
